usage: qq [-h] [--version] COMMAND ...

qq: the quirq infra command line.

Run inside a repo, qq runs the version that repo pins in infra/repo.toml.
Other qq repos add subcommands through the `qq.commands` entry point group, and a repo adds its
own with `qq create NAME COMMAND` (saved in infra/commands; then `qq NAME` runs it).

positional arguments:
  COMMAND
    sync      fetch the repo's pinned toolchains and dependencies
    fetch     clone a repo, then qq sync in it
    build     build targets here with recipes
    test      build and test targets here with recipes
    upload    push this branch and open or update its change
    try       upload, return a run ID now, push the gate's verdict later
    land      land through the gate; returns at once
    status    the gate's verdict now (exit 0 pass, 1 refused, 3 pending)
    run       run a command once, with the repo's pinned toolchains
    create    give this repo a qq command of its own (qq create NAME COMMAND)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --version   show program's version number and exit

usage: xo [-h] [--api-key KEY|-] [--url URL] [--spec FILE] [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--version]
          COMMAND ...

xo: the command line for the XO Cloud core API (dev.xo.builders/api/core/v1, through the xo server).

    xo ENDPOINT [ACTION] [--flag VALUE ...]  one command per API endpoint, made from the spec:
                                            GET /spaces/{spaceId} is `xo spaces --space-id ID` (bare
                                            `xo spaces` lists your spaces); the space creates
                                            (POST /openclaw, ...) are kinds of `xo create space`
                                            instead. Its parameters and body
                                            fields are its flags, nested fields too
                                            (--providers-anthropic-api-key); `xo ENDPOINT --help`
                                            lists them. A path with several methods has actions
                                            (list, get, create, update, replace, delete).
    xo ops [FILTER]                         list the API's operations: id, method, path, summary.
                                            FILTER keeps those whose id, path or tag contains it.
    xo call OPERATION [--param NAME=VALUE ...] [--data JSON|@FILE|-] [--field KEY=VALUE ...]
                                            run one operation from the spec. --param fills path,
                                            query and header parameters; --data or --field give the
                                            JSON body.
    xo api METHOD PATH [--query NAME=VALUE ...] [--data JSON|@FILE|-] [--field KEY=VALUE ...]
                                            send any request, spec or not. Through the xo server
                                            only the creates and GET /spaces/{id} pass; for the
                                            rest, add --url https://dev.xo.builders with
                                            $XO_API_KEY or --api-key - (not the saved key).
    xo serve [--host H] [--port P]          run the xo server: it answers `xo me` (and the admin-only
                                            /user-metadata route) with the Clerk credentials it holds,
                                            and passes the creates and GET /spaces/{id} on to XO's
                                            core API.
    xo login [xo|me|github] [--key] [--url URL]
                                            log in to every service the xo server lists (or the one
                                            named): me (the xo server) and xo take your API key, unless
                                            a saved key still works. When the xo server has browser
                                            login, you sign in to XO in your browser and the server
                                            sends your key; otherwise, with --key, or with a key piped
                                            in, it is asked for without showing it. github runs gh auth
                                            login for github.com, unless gh is already connected.
    xo status                               each service, its address, and whether you are logged in.
    xo projects [add NAME]                  show the projects list in your private metadata, or add
                                            NAME to it. The xo server makes the change and writes only
                                            that list; xo sends just the name.
    xo create project NAME [GITHUB-URL]     add a project and make its folder here. Give a name, a
                                            GitHub URL, or both: a GitHub project is called by its repo's
                                            name (headscale, from juanfont/headscale), cloned into
                                            ./headscale and listed with its owner; any other name gets
                                            `git init` (its repo can be added later wit

h xo connect
                                            NAME --repo URL).
    xo create space NAME [KIND [flags]]     with a KIND (claude-code, codex, antigravity, hermes,
                                            openclaw, xo-cowork, nebius-openclaw): create a space on XO
                                            named NAME there too, and record it in your spaces. With no
                                            KIND: this folder becomes space NAME, after you say yes: a
                                            .git with one branch per subfolder and main listing them,
                                            pushed to github.com/OWNER/NAME (public), nothing on XO.
    xo connect PROJECT SPACE [--ref R]      set PROJECT in SPACE at ref R (default main); the names
                                            need no project: or space: in front, and xo connect
                                            SPACE PROJECT works too (when both names are your
                                            projects, the one that is a space is SPACE). A
                                            PROJECT not in your projects yet (a plain name,
                                            OWNER/REPO or a GitHub URL) is added to them first;
                                            a plain name close to one of yours, or one that could
                                            be the space, needs project:NAME.
    xo connect PROJECT --repo URL           give PROJECT, made with a name only, its GitHub repo; it
                                            is recorded as OWNER/REPO and its folder becomes ./REPO.
    xo connect SPACE [--id ID]              a new space entry SPACE in your metadata (refused for a
                                            name in your projects: say space:NAME); --id ties it to
                                            an XO space you already have.
    xo list [projects | spaces | shared]    show your projects, your spaces, or the invites shared
                                            with you; with nothing after it, your projects and spaces.
    xo spaces                               the spaces linked to your account (xo list spaces); with
                                            --space-id ID, XO's connection URLs for that space.
    xo share space:S|project:P USERNAME     invite that user to a copy of the space (its name and
                                            projects) or the project.
    xo accept ID [--as NAME] [--yes]        show invite ID (from xo list shared), ask, then add a
                                            shared space as a space of your own.
    xo accept ID --space S [--ref R]        the same for a shared project: into your space S, at
                                            ref R (default main).
    xo reject ID                            take invite ID off your list (its sender can share again).
    xo install project:P | space:S          clone or fetch P here; for a space, each of its projects
                                            into ./S/ at its ref. A GitHub project's folder is its repo's
                                            name; call it by that name, or by OWNER/REPO when two of
                                            your projects share it.
    xo update project:P | space:S           push P's branch (never forced); for a space, record the
                                            refs checked out under ./S/ (refused if the space moved on).
    xo sync project:P | space:S             pull --rebase and push P; for a space, take its changes,
                                            keep yours, then record the result.
    (the xo key step:)                      ask for your API key without showing it, check it with
                                            XO through the xo server, and save it with the URL.
    xo logout                               delete the saved key, URL and addresses; asks before
                                            logging gh out of github.com.

A

request that is not a GET changes things on XO, so it prints one line on stderr first; a create
that stores your API key in the new space says so on a second line. --dry-run prints the request
and sends nothing, with provider keys and bot tokens shown as <hidden> unless --show-secrets is
given. A DELETE also needs --yes.

XO API commands go to one URL: --url, else $XO_URL, else the one xo login saved, else
https://xo.quirq.dev. The core API is under its /api/core/v1.

The API key comes from --api-key - (one line on stdin), $XO_API_KEY, or the key xo login saved,
in that order; the saved key is only ever sent to the URL it was saved with. --api-key KEY also
works but lands in your shell history and the process list. xo sends the key as a bearer token,
never prints it, and never follows a redirect. The spec comes from --spec FILE, $XO_SPEC, or the
copy bundled with xo.

Prints the response as JSON on stdout. Exit 1 on any problem, with one line on stderr saying why.

positional arguments:
  COMMAND
    ops              list the API's operations
    call             run one operation from the spec
    api              send any request (through the xo server, only the creates and GET
                     /spaces/{id} pass); non-GET changes things on XO, DELETE needs --yes
    login            log in to every service the xo server lists (me and xo with your XO API
                     key), and to GitHub with gh's login, or to the one named
    logout           delete the key and addresses xo login saved, and log gh out of github.com
                     (asked first)
    status           each service, its address, and whether you are logged in (never a key)
    serve            run the xo server that holds the Clerk credentials (see docs/server.md)
    projects         show the projects list in your private metadata, or add one (the xo
                     server makes the change and touches nothing else)
    create           create a project or a space and record it in your private metadata (the
                     xo server makes the change)
    connect          set a project's ref in one of your spaces, give a project its repo, or
                     make a new space entry
    install          clone or fetch a project here, or each of a space's projects into ./SPACE
                     at its ref
    update           push a project's branch, or record the refs checked out under ./SPACE in
                     the space (refused if the space moved on: run xo sync)
    sync             pull --rebase and push a project, or merge a space's changes with yours
                     and record the result
    share            invite a user to a copy of one of your spaces or GitHub projects (it
                     waits in their shared list until they accept or reject it)
    accept           add an invite from your shared list: a space as a space of your own, a
                     project into one of your spaces (shows what it adds and asks first)
    reject           take an invite off your shared list (its sender can share it again)
    list             show your projects and spaces, or one of them, or the invites shared with
                     you
    me               GET /me Show the account this API key belongs to (xo server)
    spaces           the spaces linked to your account; with --space-id ID, GET
                     /spaces/{spaceId} Get a space's connection URLs and sharing info (owner
                     only; URLs carry a session token)

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --api-key KEY|-    the XO API key; - reads it from stdin (default $XO_API_KEY, then the key
                     xo login saved, both safer)
  --url URL          the server XO API commands go to (default $XO_URL, then the one xo login
                     saved, then https://xo.quirq.dev)
  --spec FILE        an OpenAPI JSON file (default $XO_SPEC, then the one bundled with xo)
  --timeout TIMEOUT  seconds per request (default 30)
  --version
show program's version number and exit
